instruction: Enable the 'Do Not Track' request setting in Chrome's privacy settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome menu, navigated to Settings > Privacy and security, explored third-party cookies, site settings, on-startup page, searched 'clear on exit' in settings, then tried chrome://flags with various queries. Never found the auto-delete browsing data setting.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to chrome://settings, click sidebar sections (Privacy and security, On start-up), use settings search bar, navigate to chrome://flags and search flags
metadata.failure_analysis: Model could not locate the 'Delete browsing data on close' setting. Searched in wrong areas (cookies, site settings, flags) instead of finding the correct path in Privacy and security > clear browsing data preferences.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to enabling Do Not Track toggle, which was visible on a page the model already visited (chrome://settings/cookies). Tests model's ability to toggle a privacy setting.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling Do Not Track in Chrome. Evaluator reads Chrome Preferences file and checks enable_do_not_track boolean field.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'get_enable_do_not_track' correctly reads Chrome Preferences JSON file and extracts the 'enable_do_not_track' boolean field, returning 'true' or 'false' as a string.
Metric 'exact_match' correctly compares the getter result string against the expected value 'true' from rules.
Complete instruction coverage: the single requirement (enable Do Not Track) is fully verified by checking the preference file.
No postconfig needed since the getter reads from the on-disk Preferences file, not from UI state.
Data flow is correct: getter returns string 'true'/'false', expected is string 'true', exact_match performs correct string comparison.
